clue.text: Opportunity to spin, backing chief minister

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance

indicators.note: backing means moving in the opposite direction, so the word for spin is read from its end

parts.note: to spin or turn over is to roll

explanation.surface: A prime minister seizes a chance to put a spin on things while backing the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the Chancellor of the Exchequer is the senior cabinet minister in charge of finance; in Germany the chancellor heads the government.

clue.text: Boy gives praise in church

indicators.note: in places the word for praise inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A choirboy sings hymns of praise during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude is a male first name, and crosswords often define a first name simply as boy or girl.

clue.text: The study of sound could make one so caustic

indicators.note: could make one says the following letters can be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Studying sound might make a person sharp-tongued and bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustics is the branch of physics concerned with sound and how it travels.

clue.text: Birds caught on odd videos I released

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the usual order, so the remaining letters are jumbled
something released is let go, so that letter leaves the word it was in

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to catch them
taken as written
the letter removed

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers catch sight of something on strange videos that were let out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of VIDEOS, then rearrange the five letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Collared doves are common pigeon-like birds named for the black half-ring on the neck.

clue.text: Lake plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large lake in central Switzerland
second meaning: alfalfa, a fodder crop of the pea family

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: a Swiss lake and a forage plant share the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Lucerne is in Switzerland, and lucerne is the British name for alfalfa, grown as cattle fodder.

clue.text: Cold in Fife, so affected business premises

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for cold among the other letters
affected means changed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Cold weather in Fife hits the businesses there.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a county in eastern Scotland. The C goes in with the other letters before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices are the rooms or buildings where commercial and administrative work is done.

clue.text: Author, almost out of order

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: something amiss is wrong or out of order

explanation.surface: A writer is nearly disqualified for bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis and his son Martin Amis were both celebrated English novelists.

clue.text: Start of Mame song, or one from another musical

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the musical's title
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: The opening number of the musical Mame, or a character from a different show.
explanation.walkthrough: Mame is a Broadway musical; it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the heroine of both West Side Story and The Sound of Music, a character from another musical.

clue.text: Messy hit-and-run?

parts.note: a slap is a hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A hit-and-run driver leaves a messy scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit-and-run' reads as one motoring offence; split it into two verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means hasty and careless, so work done that way is untidy.

clue.text: First to actually tax an island

indicators.note: first to marks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of actually
a toll is a charge or tax, such as for using a road

explanation.surface: A government is the first to actually impose a tax on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Ace fare it cooked?

indicators.note: cooked means prepared by changing, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where excellent food was prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters rearrange, and the question describes a place that cooks and serves food.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant, a place where food is cooked and served.

clue.text: Savoy opera song ('lied' to her abroad)

indicators.note: abroad suggests being widely scattered, so the letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A song in an opera is called a lied when sung to a woman overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: A lied is a German art song, which fits the 'abroad' story; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas were staged at the Savoy Theatre, and The Gondoliers is one of them.

clue.text: Lose heart as pride injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged or broken, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone becomes discouraged when their pride is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all hope, the verb sense matching losing heart.

clue.text: Broadcaster's aid, line reportedly written next to character

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for line is taken by its sound

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue
a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character

explanation.surface: A presenter's prompt includes a line written beside a character in a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' and 'character' suggest a script; they are a queue and an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue card is held up off camera so a television presenter can read their lines.

clue.text: Ancient game, nim? No merriness involved

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are mixed together

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Nim is an old game, and the clue asks if it involves no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Nim really is a game of taking counters, which makes it look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine men's morris is a strategy board game for two, played since Roman times.

clue.text: Manage newspaper — good editor exhausted

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a rag is a scornful word for a newspaper
G is the abbreviation for good
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Running a newspaper wears out a good editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone run ragged has been worked until utterly tired out.

clue.text: Angler given apricots at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A fisherman out on a boat is handed some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Piscator is a literary, Latin-derived word for a fisherman, from piscis, fish.

clue.text: Such dealings may result in doing time — dash back to stop call

parts.note: someone doing time is inside, in prison

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

indicators.note: back means the word for dash is read from right to left

parts.note: to dart is to dash

explanation.surface: Shady trading can land you in jail, so dash off before a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into the wordplay: such dealings may well result in a prison sentence. The reversed dash goes after the first letter of the call word.
explanation.definitionFit: Insider trading is illegally dealing in shares using confidential company information.

clue.text: Bitterness coming out in private, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for private is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a ranker is a private, a soldier of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: Resentment shows itself in a confidential setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like secrecy; it is the army private, called a ranker in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is long-lasting resentment or bitterness towards someone.

clue.text: Great at swimming event at the seaside

indicators.note: swimming means floating about loosely, so the letters drift into another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is excellent at a swimming contest held by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming event' reads as one phrase, but swimming is the signal and event belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat or yacht races, often held on the coast.

clue.text: Part of a song about Egyptian god

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
Horus is the falcon-headed god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A section of a song concerns an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chorus is the refrain repeated between the verses of a song.

clue.text: Two vehicles boxing in a mobile home

indicators.note: boxing in means enclosing on all sides, so one letter sits between others

parts.note: a car and a van, two vehicles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two vehicles hem in a mobile home on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a vehicle towed by a car and lived in on holiday, a home on wheels.

clue.text: Turn after river close to village — take it

indicators.note: after places the word for turn behind the other pieces

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of village
a turn is a performer's act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A walker turns after the river near a village and carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take it' is the definition as in 'how did she take it?', meaning how did she respond.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to news or events, which is how someone takes it.

clue.text: Swine holding queue back is an unusually tall person

indicators.note: back means the whole combination is then read from right to left
holding means keeping something inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: a hog is a pig
a tail can be a line of waiting people or cars, as in a tailback

explanation.surface: A pig is pushing back against the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the queue word just after the H of the pig, then reverse everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant slain by David, and his name now means any giant of a person.

clue.text: Carriage entrance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: conveyance of goods or people from place to place
second meaning: the verb en-TRANCE, to fill with delight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to enchant, stressed on the second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport as a noun is conveyance, and as a verb it means to carry someone away with strong emotion.

clue.text: Composer's regal composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A composer writes a stately, kingly piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was an English composer, known for the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Measure rodent? Mouse's tail

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Mouse

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to measure a rodent by the length of a mouse's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or measure its value or quality.

clue.text: Soft drinks best therefore when daughter enters

indicators.note: enters means going inside, so the letter is placed within the others

parts.note: the cream is the best part
so means therefore
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Fizzy drinks are best, so the argument goes, when a daughter arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet, vanilla-flavoured carbonated soft drink.
